doc.title: Vancouver citation style
doc.markdown:
# Vancouver citation style
Used in medicine, nursing, public health, and most biomedical sciences. Defined by the **International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE)** and aligned with NLM (National Library of Medicine) format. Reference list is **numbered in order of first appearance**, like IEEE — but with different in-text and formatting conventions.
## In-text
- Numerals in parentheses or superscript, depending on the journal. The two most common: - Parentheses: `... has been demonstrated (3,4).` - Superscript: `... has been demonstrated.³,⁴` - Range: `(3–5)`. - Use either consistently — confirm with the target journal. Default to **parentheses** if unspecified.
## Reference list — formats by source type
### Journal article (≤ 6 authors)
``` N. Author AB, Author CD, Author EF. Article title in sentence case. Journal Abbrev. Year;Volume(Issue):Pages. doi: 10.xxxx/yyyy. ```
Example: ``` 1. Silva JP, Rocha LM, Costa AB. Cognitive training in older adults: a randomized trial. Lancet Healthy Longev. 2024;5(3):e145–e154. doi: 10.1016/S2666-7568(24)00012-3. ```
### Journal article (> 6 authors)
List first 6, then `et al.`: ``` 1. Author AB, Author CD, Author EF, Author GH, Author IJ, Author KL, et al. Title. Journal. Year;Vol(Issue):Pages. ```
### Book
``` N. Author AB. Book Title. Edition. City: Publisher; Year. ```
### Book chapter
``` N. Author AB. Chapter title. In: Editor CD, editor. Book Title. Edition. City: Publisher; Year. p. X–Y. ```
### Online article / website
``` N. Author AB. Title [Internet]. City: Publisher; Year [cited Year Mon Day]. Available from: https://url ```
### Preprint
``` N. Author AB. Title. medRxiv [preprint]. Year [cited Year Mon Day]. Available from: https://doi.org/10.xxxx/yyyy ```
### Thesis
``` N. Author AB. Title [doctoral dissertation]. City (State): University; Year. ```
### Conference proceeding
``` N. Author AB. Paper title. In: Proceedings of the Conf Name; Year Mon Day–Day; City, Country. City: Publisher; Year. p. X–Y. ```
## Author name format
- Family name + space + initials (no periods, no comma): `Silva JP`, `Rocha LM`. - Multiple authors separated by commas.
## Journal abbreviations
Use the official **NLM abbreviations** (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nlmcatalog/journals). Examples: - *The Lancet* → *Lancet* - *New England Journal of Medicine* → *N Engl J Med* - *Journal of the American Medical Association* → *JAMA* - *British Medical Journal* → *BMJ*
When in doubt, look up the journal in PubMed and copy its abbreviation from the citation export.
## Title case
- Article titles: **sentence case**, no quotes, period at end. - Journal names: abbreviated, in normal type (italics optional, journal-dependent).
## DOI
Include when available, lowercase `doi:` prefix.
## Reference managers
- **Zotero** — set output style to "Vancouver". - **EndNote** — Vancouver style is built-in. - **BibTeX** — use `\bibliographystyle{vancouver}` (requires `vancouver.bst` from CTAN). - **CSL** — Citation Style Language file `vancouver.csl` from https://www.zotero.org/styles?q=vancouver.
